messages:
Nora (ACME): Hi team — after the v3.0 rollout this morning our pricing assistant (calls to /v1/chat) started returning wrong currency conversion numbers in ~15% of cases. Previously it was fine. Example: user asks 'convert $120 USD to EUR' and model replies '€101.2' but expected ~€110. The change happened right after 08:12 UTC deploy. Any ideas? :frowning:

maria_cs: sorry to hear that, Nora. Can you paste one or two full request examples (including system/user messages) and the exact response you got? Also do you have the request ids or x-request-id headers for a few failures?

Nora (ACME): here's one sanitized example (removed customer PII):

```
POST /v1/chat
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-3.0",
  "messages": [
    {"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant that converts currencies accurately."},
    {"role":"user","content":"convert $120 USD to EUR"}
  ],
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "max_tokens": 40
}

Response:
"€101.2"

Headers: x-request-id: 0x7f3a9b22
```

maria_cs: thanks — that x-request-id is super helpful. I’ll loop in Sam from Applied ML and Devon from oncall to grab traces and check model differences. Sam, can you take a look at whether any model weight swap or tokenizer change could cause numeric conversion drift? :eyes:

sam_applied_ml: on it. Quick q: was this traffic routed to a different model variant during rollout? deploy-bot, do we have a canary routing change recorded around 08:10-08:20 UTC for customer ACME or for redwood-3.0?

deploy-bot: canary rollout for redwood-3.0 started 2026-04-20T08:05:12Z, traffic ramp 10% -> 100% completed at 2026-04-20T08:22:49Z. No per-customer override found for ACME. (trace-id: deploy-17851234)

devon_oncall: I pulled the request trace using x-request-id 0x7f3a9b22, here are relevant logs:

```
2026-04-20T08:15:03Z TRACE request 0x7f3a9b22 routed to redwood-3.0 variant a
2026-04-20T08:15:03Z DEBUG tokenizer.encode -> tokens ["convert","$","120","USD","to","EUR"]
2026-04-20T08:15:03Z DEBUG model.generate -> logits show low prob on numeric tokens
2026-04-20T08:15:03Z INFO response delivered 0x7f3a9b22
```

sam_applied_ml: interesting. Can you share the exact tokenization pieces (the token ids) and the logits slice around the numeric tokens? If ACME is comfortable, we need a couple more failing examples. Also, can you try a deterministic test with temperature 0 and top_p 1, and include the full request payload for a minimal repro? That helps rule out sampling noise.

maria_cs: Nora — could you run a quick test from your side with temperature=0, top_p=1 and paste the full response and headers if it still reproduces? If you prefer we can run a repro here but we need the exact system/user messages you used.

Nora (ACME): running now. One sec.

Nora (ACME): result with temperature=0: still "€101.2". x-request-id: 0x7f3a9b90

devon_oncall: got the new trace 0x7f3a9b90. Looks like both requests hit redwood-3.0 variant a. Sam, I attached the tokenizer ids and logits slice for the failing token positions to the incident ticket (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-4732). I also dumped the model config — no obvious change to numeric heuristics, but I do see a different vocab align compared to redwood-2.x.

sam_applied_ml: thanks. Two next steps: 1) Can someone provide a minimal repro runnable locally? e.g. exact POST body + model name + seed (if using sampling) so I can run against both redwood-2.x and redwood-3.0 to compare. 2) If we can get a handful (~5) of both correct and incorrect examples that include tokens around numbers that will let us narrow whether tokenization shifts caused the drift.

maria_cs: I drafted a minimal repro request you can paste into curl — Nora, please confirm it matches what you used (only sanitized values):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model":"redwood-3.0",
    "messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant that converts currencies accurately."},{"role":"user","content":"convert $120 USD to EUR"}],
    "temperature":0,
    "top_p":1,
    "max_tokens":20
  }'
```

Nora (ACME): confirmed, that's the exact body. I'll paste 3 more failing examples shortly.

maria_cs: perfect. Also a quick ask: please redact any internal account numbers but keep the full numeric examples (we need the numbers). If you prefer, upload the original JSONs to the secure bucket link I DM'd you.

Nora (ACME): uploaded 4 failing requests and 4 successful ones from earlier today to the bucket. Files are named acme_fail_1.json etc. I sent the link via DM.

sam_applied_ml: got the bucket access. I'm running a local compare now. Preliminary result: tokenization for "$120" changed between redwood-2.x and 3.0 — 2.x tokenized as ["$","120"] while 3.0 tokenizes as ["$120"] which shifts positional logits for subsequent tokens and seems to bias towards older exchange rates in a training artifact. Repro steps in my local env:

```
# python repro_compare.py --model old:redwood-2.9 --model new:redwood-3.0 --input "convert $120 USD to EUR" --temp 0
```

Result: old -> "€110.3"  new -> "€101.2"

maria_cs: thanks Sam. Nora — short-term we can pin ACME to redwood-2.9 while we investigate a proper fix. Would you like us to switch your tenant back to 2.9 for prod traffic? We can do a safe rollback for just your traffic.

Nora (ACME): yes please, that would be great. We can't have pricing errors in production. ETA for rollback?

devon_oncall: can do a per-tenant routing override to redwood-2.9. I will schedule it during the next maintenance window or do an immediate override if you approve. Immediate override would route all your traffic to 2.9; no downtime.

maria_cs: Nora, want immediate override now or scheduled? Also I'll open a formal bug for the tokenizer change and track model bisect & patch.

Nora (ACME): please do immediate override. Thanks all. :pray:

maria_cs: confirmed — Devon applied tenant override at 2026-04-20T09:02:10Z, ACME traffic now routed to redwood-2.9 (override-id: OV-1785123). I created ticket RINF-4732 and assigned to Sam for root cause and to infra for a model rollout guard to prevent tokenizer drift. We'll follow up with ETA in the ticket. Closing thread here but will post updates.

sam_applied_ml: plan: 1) run tokenization audit across models, 2) bisect training data & decoding code for why $+number joined tokens, 3) propose either tokenizer patch or a decoding detokenization shim to maintain numeric consistency. Will update RINF-4732 with findings.

Nora (ACME): appreciated, thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. "Passed" on pinned rollback for now. :thumbsup:

maria_cs: thanks Nora. If you see anything else, re-open this thread or DM me.
